data.narrative:
Nord Quantique, a Seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Julien Camirand Lemyre and Philippe St-Jean, has raised C$40M+ including a C$23M tranche from Quantum Champions in December 2025. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public comps (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation approach given insufficient narrow-stage peer clustering in quantum computing. Using the C$40M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a typical Seed-to-Series A step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $100M. The broader quantum computing peer set exists but lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables—only 0 same-stage and 0 adjacent-stage peers met threshold criteria—precluding reliable peer-median anchoring without introducing distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $115M (high), with $100M as the median point. This range reflects the stage-progression method alone. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer comparables at seed stage, limiting cross-validation; the impact of the recent C$23M capital raise timing on fair value; and the highly nascent, capital-intensive nature of quantum hardware development, which elevates execution risk relative to more mature software-stage cohorts.
